source_snapshot.title: Dubai to issue passports to steel, aluminium and cement. Why the city wants to extend their journey
source_snapshot.text: Dubai: Passports are no longer just for people. Dubai is set to give them to the materials that build the city, starting with steel, aluminium and cement, in an attempt to extend their journey in supporting a circular economy.At Dubai Future Week 2026, which opened on Wednesday Dubai Municipality revealed to Gulf News that Building Materials Passport will be released at the beginning of 2027.It will be mandatory for everyone in the emirate’s construction industry, including all manufacturers and suppliers, to comply, said Salama Al Suwaidi, architectural engineer at the Building Permits Department, Dubai Municipality, who presented the project at Emirates Towers..Get updated faster and for FREE: Download the Gulf News app now - simply click here..How the passport worksEach material that leaves the laboratory will have its own number, information and specifications recorded in a central system managed by the municipality. Manufacturers or suppliers must apply through the system and provide the technical details.The municipality then issues the passport based on that information. If the details do not match the required standards, the material is deemed invalid.Cement from different companies, for instance, will each carry a different passport.A life cycle that does not endUntil now, the industry has followed a linear model: materials are bought, used in construction and, once a building is demolished, taken to landfill. The new passport system is designed to turn that into a circular economy.After demolition, materials will be taken to laboratories and tested. Al Suwaidi gave the example of steel found to have 50 per cent of its strength. It would be fortified and treated so it can be used again as a new material in new buildings, an upcycling process."It's a life cycle that does not end," she said. It stops only when a material, such as a steel column, is no longer usable and must go to landfill for safety reasons.Nowhere to hideThe passport will also let authorities track what happened to specific materials after a building comes down. Those responsible for a building will be asked to account for the materials on its list of passports, including why something was not recycled after demolition. All recyclable materials from demolition sites will have to be recycled.The aims are to reduce reliance on imported materials, cut costs, lower carbon emissions and make construction more sustainable.In the initial phase, the system will cover just the three materials, but Al Suwaidi said the ambition is to target everything eventually.Dubai Future Week 2026, organised by the Dubai Future Foundation, runs till November 21 at Emirates Towers and the Museum of the Future. With the theme 'For the Future Human', the event brings together more than 10,000 participants, including experts, decision-makers, policymakers and innovators..Dubai unveils AI platform D.Mind to tackle residents’ complaints with quick solutions.Dubai launches “City AI Agent” to understand residents' needs and revolutionise services .Sheikh Hamdan launches Dubai’s Dh325 million 'Seed of Hope' campaign to support cancer patients.Dubai calls on global innovators to turn 37 city challenges into 10 projects in 90 days

source_verification.reason: All factual claims in the post are directly supported by the source text.

claims.claim: Dubai will introduce passports for steel, aluminium, and cement starting early 2027.
The passports will contain technical data and track the usage of these materials.
It is mandatory for all manufacturers and suppliers in Dubai's construction industry to comply with this requirement.
The system will enable recycling of materials after building demolition and support a circular economy, reducing emissions and costs.
There are plans to expand the program to cover all construction materials in the future.

title: Dubai to issue passports to steel, aluminium and cement. Why the city wants to extend their journey
summary_ru: 🚧 Дубай введёт паспорта для стали, алюминия и цемента В Дубае с начала 2027 года строительные материалы получат паспорта, которые будут содержать технические данные и отслеживать их использование. Это обязательное требование для всех производителей и поставщиков в строительной отрасли эмирата. Система позволит перерабатывать материалы после сноса зданий и поддерживать циклическую экономику, снижая выбросы и затраты. В дальнейшем планируется расширить программу на все строительные материалы.
